symbols.name: first input value
symbols.meaning: The first of the two input values of the butterfly.
symbols.quote: Let $\xi$ and $\zeta$ be the two input values, which the paper calls $u$ and $v$.

symbols.name: second input value
symbols.meaning: The second of the two input values of the butterfly.
symbols.quote: Let $\xi$ and $\zeta$ be the two input values, which the paper calls $u$ and $v$.

symbols.name: butterfly map
symbols.meaning: The two-point map sending a pair of values to its half-sum and half-difference.
symbols.quote: $H_0$ is the two-point map that sends a pair to its half-sum and half-difference: $H_0(\xi,\zeta)=\left(\frac{\xi+\zeta}{2},\frac{\xi-\zeta}{2}\right)$.

symbols.name: index bit
symbols.meaning: The index of one bit of a position, counted from 0 at the least significant end, so a level acts on the pairs that differ in this bit.
symbols.quote: Write each position as $\log_2 q$ bits, and let $\sigma$ be the index of one bit, counting from $0$ at the least significant end.

relations.quote: The butterfly is an elementary step of the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), the two-point map that replaces a pair of values by their half-sum and half-difference.
The butterfly is followed by a signed [Cyclic shift](cyclic-shift.md) of each record, which rotates the coefficients and negates those that wrap around.
